name: Liftoff
design_intent:
ORBIT circuit, slot 3 (diff 3). Lesson: ESCAPE VELOCITY -- boost AGAINST radial gravity to break out of the well. One moon (body_r 200, field r 900, g 1350, visual moon) centered at (960,400); the north-pole surface sits at y=200 and the field edge straight up is at y=-500. The goal_gate + a small trampoline landing pad hang ABOVE the field edge, centered at y=-760 (gate spans y -910..-610), i.e. ~110-260px OUTSIDE the pull. You spawn on the pole (start_gate 960,140) and must climb straight out of the well.

FLIGHT-REQUIRED / movement-tool-per-gap: the surface-to-goal climb is 200 -> -610 = 810px of straight-up travel, and 700px of that is INSIDE the r900 field fighting a 1350 pull. A passive bounce cannot escape: trampoline apex 270 reaches only y=-70 (deep inside the field) and spring apex 480 reaches y=-280 (still ~220px short of the field edge at -500), so ANY un-boosted bounce decays back to the moon. Only a sustained radial boost (boost_gravity_scale 0.8 while thrusting grants climb authority; ~26.6px per fuel) carries you through the field boundary and up to the pad -- the purest 'flight, not bounce' gate in the circuit. A climb that runs out short falls safely back to the moon (retry, fuel refunds on landing); overshooting sideways past the field into global-down drops out the bottom bound = free respawn. Bounds top -1600 clears a super apex from the pad footing; ~660px side margins.
hint: BOOST STRAIGHT UP — ESCAPE THE PULL TO THE PAD
